note: Narration templates for the guided tours. Figures come from {placeholders} filled from the live data; conclusions are chosen by rules in the app ({"by": fact, "cases": {...}}). The weekly tour agent may refine wording and choose examples, within the rules checked by tools/validate.py.

gap.title: Is AI shrinking the gap from research to change?

intro.say: Each arc is a research breakthrough, from a university, a government lab or industry. It rises when the research began, lands at the first product, and a thinner arc runs on to large-scale adoption.

yes: For example: {exTitle}. Research {exWhere} began in {exR}, the first product came in {exP}

cases.yes: , and it was in mainstream use by {exAdopt}.

cases.no: Select any arc to see its story.

say: Here is a century of change. Thinner arcs carry on to mainstream adoption

cases.shrunk: Overall, the gap has shrunk: {pre} years before 1970, {recent} since 2000.
cases.grown: Overall, the gap has grown: {pre} years before 1970, {recent} since 2000.
cases.flat: Overall, the gap has barely changed: {pre} years before 1970, {recent} since 2000.
cases.unclear: There is not yet enough data to say how the gap has changed overall.

say: But recent research has not all landed yet. Allowing for work still unfinished,

cases.holds: the shrinking holds, at about {kmYears} years.
cases.weakens: research since 2010 takes about {kmYears} years, so the improvement is smaller.
cases.tooEarly: it is too early to be sure.
cases.unclear: there is not yet enough data to tell.

gapchart.say: The gap-over-time chart follows this decade by decade, then adds scenarios beyond today, including AI and digital twins.

cases.ai: Since 2000, AI itself is the fastest field, at about {fastestYears} years.
cases.other: Since 2000, {fastestName} is fastest; AI ranks {aiRankWord} of {nFields}.

say: With one field selected, its sub-fields get their own tracks.

cases.faster: Since 2010, AI-driven work took {ai} years, against {oth} for the rest.
cases.slower: Since 2010, AI-driven work has taken longer: {ai} years, against {oth}.
cases.similar: Since 2010, AI-driven work took about as long as the rest: {ai} years against {oth}.
cases.unclear: There are not yet enough AI-driven milestones to compare.

cases.faster: Ahead, AI-assisted work is expected to take {aiOut} years, against {convOut}.
cases.slower: Ahead, the estimates do not show AI landing sooner.

say: So, is AI shrinking the gap?

cases.0: Not yet: the data do not show it.
cases.1: Partly: some of the evidence says yes.
cases.2: Probably: most of the evidence says yes.

say: The answer updates as new evidence arrives.

horizon.title: What AI-assisted products are on the horizon for the energy system?

intro.say: DESNZ's vision for an AI-enabled clean energy system groups the opportunities into five areas. Diamonds mark the arcs linked to them, playing here from 1980.

radar.say: The Vision radar shows how ready each area's technologies are: {nResearch} in research, {nPilot} piloting, {nCommercial} in first commercial use and {nScale} at scale. {nGB} are deployed in Great Britain.

cases.some: In the last three months the agents found {newCount} new, including {newTitle}. Mark them as reviewed, and next time you see only what has arrived since.
cases.none: Nothing new has arrived in the last three months. Mark the radar as reviewed, and next time you see only what has arrived since.

cases.some: Within five years, {nextCount} are expected, the soonest being {nextTitle}, around {nextYear}. {busiestArea} has the most in the pipeline.
cases.none: No arrivals are expected within five years in the current data.

changes.say: Data changes lists everything the agents add or correct each week. Here it shows only changes linked to the vision.

slide.say: For a briefing, the PowerPoint report window creates a one-slide summary of all five areas, ready to drop into a deck.

say: So, what is on the horizon?

cases.busy: A busy pipeline: much of it is already piloting, and the radar shows where it is landing first.
cases.steady: A steady pipeline, with the radar showing which areas are moving.
cases.quiet: Not much yet in the data, so watch the radar as the agents search each week.

intro.say: New technology brings new ways in. Of the technologies here, {attackPct} percent expand the attack surface, from smart devices at the grid edge to AI agents.

say: The Cyber lens shows how long security took to catch up: typically

cases.slow: {lag} years after a technology arrived, a long time to be exposed.
cases.fast: within {lag} years of a technology arriving.
cases.unclear: it is not yet clear from the data.

cases.some: {gapCount} technologies arrived since 2010 with no security response in their category yet, such as {gapTitle}.
cases.none: Every technology since 2010 has seen a security response in its category, at least in this data.

example.say: Each card names the risk and suggests mitigations, linked to the NCSC CAF, Ofgem's CAF Overlay, NIST, NERC CIP and IEC 62443.

cases.some: A guidance agent records new security guidance every week, CAF and Ofgem first. The latest: {guideTitle}.
cases.none: A guidance agent records new security guidance every week, CAF and Ofgem first.

caution.say: This is AI research to prompt discussion, not security advice. Always engage qualified experts, and your regulator where relevant.

cases.improving: It is catching up faster than it used to.
cases.worsening: It is taking longer to catch up than it used to.

intro.say: Research does not just change products; it makes fortunes. Time to a fortune follows founders from starting a company to the listing, sale or valuation that made them rich.

research.say: Of {nFortunes} fortunes here, {nResearch} began in a university or research lab. Gold rings mark those research founders.

cases.faster: The road is getting shorter: about {preYears} years for companies founded before 1970, and {recentYears} for those founded since 2015.
cases.slower: The road is getting longer: about {preYears} years before 1970, and {recentYears} since 2015.
cases.similar: The road is about as long as ever: {preYears} years before 1970, {recentYears} since 2015.
cases.unclear: There are not yet enough recent fortunes to compare eras.

fastest.say: Sorted by speed, the fastest so far is {fastestCo}, in {fastestTime}.

cases.faster: Filter by country: research that began in the UK reached a product in {ukYears} years, faster than the {rowYears} elsewhere.
cases.slower: Filter by country: research that began in the UK took {ukYears} years to reach a product, against {rowYears} elsewhere.
cases.similar: Filter by country: UK research reached a product in about the same time as elsewhere, {ukYears} years against {rowYears}.
cases.unclear: Filter by country to compare UK research with the rest of the world.

uni.say: University projects still under way carry a gold ring: {nUni} of them, the next generation of breakthroughs and perhaps fortunes.

table.say: The Table lists every milestone. Sort by any column, such as the gap, and select a row for its story.

cases.similar: the journey takes about as long as ever.
cases.unclear: the data will tell as more fortunes are made.

intro.say: This model is maintained by AI agents that run every week. It holds {nMilestones} milestones so far.

research.say: A research agent searches each field, and each DESNZ vision area, for new breakthroughs and products. Data changes lists everything it adds.

qa.say: A second agent checks every find independently. It needs two sources, and the quoted evidence must really appear on the page. Nothing is ever deleted.

more.say: Two more agents track new security guidance and refresh these walk-throughs. Every change must pass automatic checks before it is published.

say: Data quality shows {pctSourceCited} percent of records now cite a checked source.

cases.scored: Forecasts are scored as they land: {fcResolved} so far.
cases.none: Each forecast is recorded, and will be scored as it lands.

labels.say: Every record says how it was checked: source-cited, AI-compiled or an AI estimate. You can filter by these.

arrange.say: Arrangements set the windows up for exploring, presenting, analysis or a DESNZ briefing. You can save any view, or share it as a link.

answer.say: Help and the i buttons explain everything. It is AI-maintained, so it may contain errors: check anything important against the sources.
